issue: Does a conviction for conspiracy under 21 U.S.C. § 846, which does not require an overt act, qualify as a 'controlled substance offense' under the Guidelines career-offender provision, given that Application Note 1 includes conspiracy and generic conspiracy requires an overt act?

sides.position: A § 846 conspiracy is not a controlled substance offense because it lacks the overt-act element of generic conspiracy, creating a categorical mismatch with the Guidelines commentary.
cases: United States v. McCollum, 885 F.3d 300 (4th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Whitley, 737 F. App'x 147 (4th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Martinez-Cruz, 836 F.3d 1305 (10th Cir. 2016)

sides.position: A § 846 conspiracy conviction qualifies as a controlled substance offense; the lack of an overt-act element does not create a categorical mismatch.
cases: United States v. Rivera-Constantino, 798 F.3d 900 (9th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Sanbria-Bueno, 549 F. App'x 434 (6th Cir. 2013)
United States v. Rodriguez-Escareno, 700 F.3d 751 (5th Cir. 2012)

quote: There is no controlling authority on this issue in this circuit, and the other circuits remain divided in their response to it.
cite: United States v. Lewis, 963 F.3d 16 (1st Cir. 2020)
